text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Zambia is to increase its crude oil storage facilities with the installation of storage tanks for 30,000 tonnes, energy minister Suresh Desai said on Sunday.
- The central bank last week rejected treasury bill tenders because of high interest rates attached to the bids by commercial banks and has restricted all fresh bids to 50 percent interest.
- A parliamentarians' environmental workshop has recommended that parliament enact laws to regulate the use of natural resources.

- President Frederick Chiluba's lawyers have objected to an application by the Post -- an independent newspaper -- that he undergo a DNA test to determine whether he fathered a child outside wedlock with a Zairean woman. The newspaper made the application in a case in which the president has sued it for libel.
